scope: Complete visible exterior observational approximation of NYCU Guangfu Rolling Pavilion, 2024 photographic state; not exact NURBS or surveyed reproduction.
source_evidence: Designer first-party complete decoded photographs; official Taipei Design Award identification and 8m span/4.8m height; private image integrity/EXIF manifest retained outside public package.
accepted_features: Skewed open shell with right returning curve rather than symmetric barrel
Paired narrow ladder-like primary bands; short transverse rungs kept inside bands, not spanning whole skin
Larger front opening and smaller open rear aperture
Front one-sided curled seat with broadened low horizontal toe and fascia
Separate low transverse rear bench, not a mirrored curled front seat
Milky film display and warm dark bamboo are disclosed approximations
No added rear wall, central columns, neighboring buildings or hidden footings
iteration_corrections: Rejected initial barrel silhouette and separate chair-like seat
Corrected full-shell slats to ladder-band-local rungs
Corrected rear aperture over-shrinking and brown material-transfer triangles
remaining_limits: Eight principal bands are photo interpretation, not an as-built count schedule
Exact spline control points, varying profiles, seat plan, rib depth and geometry remain approximated
Film thickness and transparency are display/exchange surrogates; ordinary STL does not reproduce translucency
Fine rung count, bamboo laminations, knots, fasteners and below-ground foundations not reconstructed
Top view is an internally consistent model view, not supported by a surveyed roof plan
No independent conclusion on structural integrity, manufacturing wall thickness, support-free printing or real print success
No claim that 2024 images verify physical state in 2026
documentation_review: README.md and SOURCES.md reviewed; requested correction of magazine name from 建築師雜誌 to 台灣建築. This naming correction does not affect geometric review.
hash_scope_note: Review binds listed geometry/generator/render artifacts. Subsequent artifact changes require fresh review; no claim of reviewing other future hashes.
